My question in append and extend we are inserting single value,but in extend the single value inputs is passed as multiple single values,concept wise I am ok,what is the use case of doing like this in extend method ,can someone explain?
a string is an iterable object
so when you pass it in via extends, it doesn’t add it wholesale
extends iterates over the passed in iterable and adds each index of that iterable to the original list
append just adds the new object to the list

Hi guys, happy new year everybody! I’m trying to print out to the console only 10 URLs from the long ‘loc’ list -what am i doing wrong? :sparkles:
`for url in soup.find_all('loc'):`
`    for x in range(1, 10):`
`        print(url.text)`
`        x += 1`
I assume it’s printing out each url ten times?
yeap
well, actually, no, your `x += 1` kinda borks that as well

so try this instead:
```
for url in soup.find_all('loc')[:10]:
    print(url.text)
```
thnx <@Zack>
did it work?
yeap
cool - so the key there is that `soup-find_all` is returning a list, which you can slice, only taking the first 10 elements using that `[:10]` notation
soz for lame q btw
not lame
one bit you might have been confused on though is that iterating using the inner `for` loop was just using the same value for `url` each time.
and further, the `x += 1` wasn’t necessary, because `x` changed automatically for each iteration of that for loop
